scope: Resolve the three remaining failures in the six-file custom-element validation. Application validation remains limited to docs/wistia-custom-elements-selection.json; no broad samples or runtime comparisons were resumed.

fixes.change: Resolve scalar vw/vh/vmin/vmax lengths in computed styles. Preserve authored inline units and unsupported expressions. Cache keys include owner document and viewport dimensions so inherited values and iframe/adoption results refresh correctly.

fixes.issue: Drawer cleanup restored empty inline overflow, but computed overflow stayed empty
fixes.change: Provide the initial computed overflow value visible; ignore empty standard declarations so authored stylesheet overflow still applies after inline restoration. Application scroll-lock/cleanup behavior is unchanged.

fixes.issue: The real lazy UI component prevented the lifecycle fixture from completing in both environments
fixes.change: Use a controlled deferred component for the mocked entry point. Preserve the before/after mount-marker assertions, deferred import and rendered-child checks; the child label also verifies prop delivery. Production React/custom-element and InputPassword components are unchanged.
fixes.coverage_scope: The lifecycle unit test no longer covers the real InputPassword UI implementation; it isolates the custom-element/lazy-mount contract.

mandatory_fork_commit_hook.note: Existing repository coverage/conformance gate runs automatically on source commits.

remaining_limits: Viewport resolution covers scalar length values. calc()/min()/max()/clamp(), percentages, container units and the full layout engine remain unsupported or unchanged.
Only the overflow shorthand initial value is supplied; this does not add a full CSS initial-value catalog or overflow-axis coupling.
Computed styles retain the runtime snapshot/cache model; complete browser-live CSSStyleDeclaration behavior is not implemented.
Customized built-ins, ElementInternals, scoped registries and other previously documented autonomous-custom-element limitations remain.
No new end-to-end performance claims; the comparison remains stopped.
